messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU queue growth detected in prod-us-west-2. Pending pods: 472, Avg queue wait ~65s, tokenized requests backing up to API gateway. Autoscaler failing to provision additional GPU nodes. Paging sam (oncall-sre).

sam (oncall-sre): Saw the pager. Looking at CA logs now. Can someone paste the ASG/limits?

marta (infra): ASG gpu-prod-2 currently at desired 16, min 4, max 16. We've hit max. No new instances will be launched until max increased.

sam (oncall-sre): OK that's the immediate limit. But cluster-autoscaler logs also show launch template errors earlier. Pasting snippet: ```W0213 14:12:09.123456 1 scale_up.go:467] Failed to increase size of ASG gpu-prod-2: *awserrors.InvalidLaunchTemplate: LaunchTemplateId 'lt-0abc1234' version '3' not found```

jin (eng-runtime): That matches the deploy we rolled out last night; new LT version pinned for GPU images and the autoscaler IAM role might not have passRole. CA tried to create spot instances with the new template and got 403s in the cloud provider plugin logs: ```ERROR: AccessDenied: iam:PassRole```.

sam (oncall-sre): So two things: (1) ASG max cap preventing scaling, (2) launch template/iam errors preventing new launches even if we increase cap. We need infra to update the ASG max and validate LT, and SRE to orchestrate temporary mitigation to unblock pending pods.

marta (infra): I'm increasing ASG max to 24 now (manual bump). Should take effect within a minute. Also rolling back launch template version to v2 which the ASG previously used? Would that be acceptable?

jin (eng-runtime): v2 is compatible with kernel modules we need. Yes please roll ASG to use version 2. But we also need the instance profile to include the autoscaler IAM role (or allow PassRole). I'll verify the instance profile mapping.

sam (oncall-sre): While infra works on ASG/LT, I'm going to reduce pressure on the queue: scaling down heavy model replicas in prod to free up GPUs and enable partial service. Lee, can support throttle some non-critical workloads / background batch jobs?

lee (support): Noted. We'll mute low-priority ingestion pipelines and flip the feature-flag for nightly-batch. Pushing changes now.

ops-bot: action: feature-flag toggled -> nightly-batch: OFF by lee at 14:14 UTC :white_check_mark:

sam (oncall-sre): CA logs after ASG bump (tail): ```I0213 14:15:30.987654 1 aws_manager.go:345] Increase size request for ASG gpu-prod-2 to 20 accepted```. But still seeing launchtemplate error for v3.

marta (infra): Confirmed: ASG updated to max 24 and attempted scale to 20. I'm switching ASG LaunchTemplate version to 2 and updating instanceProfile to attach role autoscaler-node-role. Doing now.

marta (infra): Done. ASG now uses LaunchTemplate v2. Instance profile attached. 

sam (oncall-sre): Re-watching CA logs... ```I0213 14:18:03.112233 1 scale_up.go:512] Scale-up: launching 4 nodes for pending pods```. Nice.

sam (oncall-sre): However, several nodes are arriving NotReady with kubelet errors: ```kernel module nvidia not found```. Looks like a kernel mismatch on the newer AMI in LT v2. Pods still pending with reasons: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu and TolerationMissing: taint key gpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule.

jin (eng-runtime): That taint is applied by our node-setup DaemonSet to reserve some nodes for critical model shards. If the node setup fails, taint doesn't get applied, or if it does, pods without toleration get rejected. We should check the node bootstrap logs.

sam (oncall-sre): I'm SSHing into one of the new nodes. Journal shows failure to mount nvidia drivers. Quick fix option: roll forward to AMI with pre-baked drivers or force a rolling restart of the nodepool with correct AMI. But that's heavy. Another lighter mitigation: temporarily remove the gpu-reserved taint from the relevant nodegroup so pending pods can schedule. That reduces isolation but will unblock traffic.

marta (infra): We can remove taint annotation via nodegroup config in ASG user-data? Easier: run kubectl taint nodes -l eks.amazonaws.com/nodegroup=gpu-prod-2 gpu-reserved:NoSchedule- to remove at node level. Doing that for the 4 new nodes to let pods land. ETA ~2m.

sam (oncall-sre): Do it. Also run `kubectl describe pod` for a sample pending pod to confirm reasons.

marta (infra): taint removal complete. 

ops-bot: command: kubectl taint nodes -l eks.amazonaws.com/nodegroup=gpu-prod-2 gpu-reserved:NoSchedule- executed by marta at 14:22 UTC :white_check_mark:

sam (oncall-sre): Pods are now binding and scheduling to GPUs. Queue backlog dropping from 472 -> 210 in the last 6m. Latency tail improved to ~28s. Keep watching.

lee (support): Notifying affected customers: sending initial incident notification to enterprise customers (prod tenant 4 and 9) — impact: degraded throughput and elevated latency for GPU-backed endpoints, partial request failures for large-batch jobs. ETA for full recovery: 2 hours (TBD).

lee (support): Message posted to status page draft -> https://status.example.com/incidents/draft/1969991111 (link).

sam (oncall-sre): Good. We still need root cause follow-up: 1) why LT v3 went missing/was invalid in ASG, 2) why the AMI drifted causing missing drivers, 3) why instance profile didn't allow PassRole. I'll open a post-incident ticket and assign to infra + runtime.

marta (infra): Creating infra ticket: INF-6821 referencing ASG config drift and LT bookkeeping. Adding logs and CloudTrail events showing a failed LT publish during last night's deploy.

jin (eng-runtime): Creating runtime ticket: RNT-3380 for AMI bake pipeline and driver bootstrapping failures. Also will add a healthcheck for kernel module presence in node readiness probe.

sam (oncall-sre): Summary for pager: cause = capacity exhaustion + multi-factor autoscaler failure (ASG max cap + invalid launch template + AMI driver mismatch + node taint blocking). Mitigations applied: increased ASG max, rolled ASG to LT v2, attached instance profile, removed gpu-reserved taint to allow scheduling, throttled background jobs, and monitoring queue. Current status: partial recovery, queue draining, no data loss but degraded latency.

pager: Incident declared SEV2 at 14:25 UTC. Handoff to marta for infra remediation. Oncall sam continues monitoring for 2 hours.

lee (support): Sent customer update to enterprise mailing list and workspace channels. Customers asked for ETA and will be updated hourly.

marta (infra): Adding temporary guardrails: setting ASG max to 32 until we complete root cause and bake a new validated LT/AMI. Also creating an automated check to prevent deploys that do not update instance profile passrole mapping.

sam (oncall-sre): Thanks team. Keeping thread open for any new errors. I'll capture timeline and attach logs to the issue. If queue stops dropping or pods crash, we escalate to exec incident.

jin (eng-runtime): Note for follow-up: add a CA integration test to simulate launch template version mismatch and ensure graceful fallback to previous template.

lee (support): next customer update sent 14:55 UTC: queue at 120, estimated further 30–45m to baseline.

sam (oncall-sre): last check at 14:55 UTC: pending 98, tail latency 22s. Marking incident as mitigated but will remain open for remediation tasks and postmortem.

incidents-bot: incident update: mitigated -> service degraded -> follow-up tickets created: INF-6821, RNT-3380.

sam (oncall-sre): Closing active pager. Assigning postmortem to sam + marta + jin.

marta (infra): I'll schedule emergency change window to validate AMI bake and LT publishing pipeline tomorrow morning.

lee (support): I'll keep communications cadence until all remediation tasks are finished.

sam (oncall-sre): thanks everyone :clap: staying on-call for next 60m, then handing to next shift.

ops-bot: handoff: sam -> marta at 16:00 UTC :handshake:
